The question asks about the timing of the arrival of the people who first settled the Delaware Valley relative to the country that produced the television show **@Seven**.  
**@Seven** was a New Zealand‑produced comedy series (broadcast by TV3). The “people who first settled the Delaware Valley” – i.e., the European colonists who established a presence along the Delaware River in what is now the United States – arrived in the early‑to‑mid‑17th century:

| Region / Colony | Earliest European Activity | Years |
|-----------------|---------------------------|-------|
| Swedish New Sweden | 1638 (first settlement on Eleuthera Island) | 1638‑1655 |
| Dutch (New Amsterdam) | 1635 (initial forays), main settlement 1639 | 1639‑1654 |
| English (Pennsylvania) | 1664 (England captures New Sweden; later William Penn’s charter 1681) | 1664‑1681 |

Hence, the Delaware Valley’s first European settlers came to North America roughly **260–300 years before the New Zealand‑produced show @Seven** (which aired 21 December 2009 – 22 January 2010).

In short: the settlers never “came to the country that produced @Seven” – they settled in what is now the United States in the early 1600s, whereas @Seven was filmed and aired in New Zealand almost 300 years later.
